intelligence.human_view: Think of joining like meeting a new friend. Ten questions, asked warmly — who are you, what do you love, what can you do for people — and your answers, in your own words, become your page. Nobody asks you to prove you are good at what you are good at; they take your word for it, the way a friend would. You type it, or you speak it, or you skip it — whatever you put in is what shows, one frame at a time, and anything you leave blank simply stays hidden until you feel like adding it. Every little feature has a tiny "i" next to it that tells you, in the simplest words, what it does. Your private notes stay private until you choose to put one in a post and share it. And the whole system is built the same way: we make our own pages first, make them incredible, and those become the pattern for everybody — one page built once, then copied with new words for a person, a business, a world.

intelligence.naya_view: Build the walk on the ten stamped questions, in order: name · motto · vision · goal · mission · love / don't love · your thing · values + laws · declaration · what can you do for people. Distill each answer to its essence by default; the citizen edits after. Skills is its own lens: what can you do for people — what you offer, your ability, your service, your unique ability, what you give to the world. Per skill ask only what it does for them and how someone starts — never proof at join; strike "proof" from the walk-questions draft and from any Skills brief that still carries it. Build the Skills page as a résumé: who you are at the top, then the headline statement — "this is what I have to offer and this is what I'm looking to do for you" — then experiences, if they want them. Business: "here's my services." Person: "this is what I'm good at." End in connection, not necessarily a sale: "connect with me, I'm good at XYZ." Input is boxes, one per question, with dictation and skip on each — same experience as the join walkthrough, just framed; show whatever they input, frame by frame, unedited. Main page: ask Naya to write it and paste it, or write it yourself, or dictate it — click enter, live on the intelligent board, showcased. Render a frame only when its answer exists; a blank renders nothing, never a placeholder. Settings lists every available area with add-a-template-block for each. Put a little "i" beside every feature — simplest-words explanation on tap; on Post a note the "i" says: personal daily notes to yourself, private by default, not for the world. A note goes public only through "add note to post" on a post — never build a separate Smart Note / Naya Note creation row. Max only: let the citizen move any frame before another; the frame set never changes, only the sequence; Power and Pro keep the template order. Build Naya's own About and Skills first, to the incredible bar — an interface within an interface, the ultimate high tech interface within the digital kingdom — before the template goes to anyone else. Build the three examples filled: Shawn (Personal), NayaNet (Business), connecting like minds (World) — each with cover, About, Skills. Finish the Universal Smart App once, on Personal, About and Skills filled from what we know about Shawn, formatting beautiful and right — he edits after. Then clone it for Business and World, changing only text, image, video, and button labels. Never rebuild a page that already exists; a rebuild brief is out of alignment — the brief names the clone source instead. Start with the fourteen: Shawn and the thirteen Nayas.
